about.title: About the Village
about.lead: {{village}} is a small village in northwestern Bulgaria, at the foot of Stara Planina (the Balkan Mountains).

sections.heading: Geographic Location
sections.body: The village of {{village}} is located in {{municipality}} Municipality, {{province}} Province, about {{distanceBerkovitsa}} km northwest of the town of Berkovitsa, {{distanceMontana}} km southwest of the city of Montana, and approximately {{distanceSofia}} km northwest of Sofia. The terrain is foothill country, covered with beech and oak forests, with an average elevation of {{elevation}} meters.

sections.heading: Origin of the Name
sections.body: The name "{{village}}" derives from the Old Bulgarian verb "kutam" — to hide, to conceal. The village is indeed tucked away by the Zlatitsa River, amid several valleys, which for a long time kept it off the radar of chroniclers and writers — hidden, yet enduring.

sections.heading: History
sections.body: The area around the village holds traces of an ancient settlement — not far away lie the remains of Kotenovtsi Fortress and a Thracian sanctuary, testament to the centuries-old history of this land at the foot of Stara Planina. The population of {{village}} has never exceeded 1,000 people, and the village has suffered devastation from disease and invasion at least three times throughout its history — each time rising again, like the phoenix.

sections.heading: Localities and Nature
sections.body: The Zlatitsa River flows past the village — described by locals as "as golden as it is bloody," owing to the vicissitudes of history. The surrounding area is dotted with places bearing evocative names: Zdravitsa, Zdravchenitsa, Tserovski Peak and Tserovski Valley, as well as Mŭrtvini — shaded spots where sunlight rarely reaches. Beech and oak forests encircle the village, and its proximity to Stara Planina makes it a starting point for travelers seeking clean air, mountain trails, and tranquility far from the noise of the city.

sections.heading: Traditions and Culture
sections.body: {{village}} is known for its celebrated brass band music, its wealth of folk songs, and its haiduk traditions. Hard work and patience are considered defining traits of the local people — qualities forged by the demanding life of the mountain region.

attractions.title: Attractions
attractions.lead: Discover the historical and natural treasures of {{village}} and its surroundings.

items.title: Thracian Sanctuary and Fortress
items.text: On a hill above the village stands a complex that researchers describe as a "cult site, sanctuary, fortress, settlement" — covering an area of about one decare (0.1 hectare). Excavations at the start of the last century uncovered a marble relief of the Thracian Horseman, a relief of a forest nymph, and Roman coins. The site is presumed to date from the Roman era.
items.citation: V. Dobruski, "The Thracian Horsemen and Other Rider Gods" (1907)

items.title: Church of the Ascension of Christ
items.text: The village church, built in 1863 — the spiritual heart of Kotenovtsi for more than a century and a half, and a witness to the National Revival era in this mountain region.

items.title: The Zlatitsa River
items.text: The river by which the village is tucked away — locals describe it as "as golden as it is bloody." Its name is no accident: gold was once panned from its riverbed.

items.title: Tserovski Peak and Tserovski Valley
items.text: Picturesque localities in the surrounding area, part of the network of trails through the beech and oak forests of Stara Planina.

items.title: Zdravitsa and Zdravchenitsa
items.text: Localities named after zdravets (geranium) — a symbol of health and blessing in Bulgarian tradition.

items.title: Trails in Stara Planina
items.text: Routes through beech and oak forests, ideal for hiking and nature watching.

items.title: Traditional Village Architecture
items.text: Authentic stone and timber houses, characteristic of villages in northwestern Bulgaria.
